analysis.title: US Equity Strategy - 4Q26 Outlook - S&P 500: $40tn Build AI, Sell AI, Use AI vs $40tn US Debt
key_insights: SG sets a year-end 2026 S&P 500 target of 8,000, which is 20x on $400 EPS. SG says the index has derated about 20%, that the market overprices macro fear and underprices micro strength, and that profits remain the glue.
Bull case: oil $80, 10-year UST at 4% and an AI cash-flow inflection take the S&P 500 to 10,000. Bear case: oil $150, UST at 6% and no hyperscaler free cash flow inflection take it to 6,000.
SG's view is two more Fed hikes, with the Fed unlikely to get ahead of the curve and no curve inversion. SG describes central banks as in mid-cycle hikes while staying behind the curve.
SG says all booms end with a bond shock but the US is not there yet. A 5% US 10-year reflects nominal growth, while 6% UST combined with $150 oil risks a micro credit event.
SG says US bonds become more attractive than US stocks if yields rise another 50bps. The US equity risk premium gets stretched if the 10-year yield rises 50-60bps.
SG says the US needs a 2.3% yield to stabilize debt/GDP levels.
Fed hikes pause the broadening trade. Equal Weight tends to de-rate as the Fed tightens, and SG recommends pausing Equal Weight.

In past Fed hiking episodes, the 3-month sector returns afterward were Energy +6.6%, Telecom +2.8%, Technology +2.3% and Industrials +1.5%, while Financials returned -3.4%. SG's curve view favors Tech, Industrials and Energy.
SG is long large caps, Tech, Industrials and Energy, and short US regional banks (KRE).
Tech has the cheapest PEG ratio globally even after 9x returns. SG describes the Tech boom as profit driven.
The AI ecosystem is about $40tn, roughly 60% of the S&P 500. SG splits it into Build AI ($17tn, 62 stocks), Sell AI ($16tn, 23 stocks) and Use AI ($9tn, 31 stocks).

Hyperscalers (Google, Meta, Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon) face a $200bn 2027 funding gap. SG says to watch their CDS rather than EPS, and recommends long US Hyperscalers CDS. Hyperscaler CDS has suppressed equity valuations.
Hyperscaler capex keeps rising through 2028, but its growth rate slows from 1H27. Free cash flow should inflect in 2H27.
Cloud backlog jumped by about $300bn quarter on quarter across Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle.

Semis EBITDA margins are at new highs, and the market is pricing peak margins. KOSPI forward P/E is about 50% below its long-run average, so a 50% EPS fall is priced in. SG says forced deleveraging in Korean single-stock leveraged ETFs is done, with assets under management halved.
Dispersion is high between spenders and beneficiaries: SG's AI Capex Beneficiaries basket is up 69% against hyperscalers up 2%.

SG US Reshoring Beneficiary index is up 17% YTD. There have been $5.2tn of US onshore investment announcements since 2025, 60% in tech and 40% (about $2tn) in onshoring. AI capex is about 1% of US GDP.

Midterm scenarios: a Democrat sweep makes Trump a lame duck and is not a positive catalyst for the AI trade and defense. A Democratic House with a Republican Senate is net a positive catalyst for AI and defense.

Commodities: SG raised its oil floor from $55 to $79 and is long gold and copper. Gold is projected at $6,666 on a debasement thesis. SG is bullish on copper, with a 2027 LME price of $15,125/t and growing deficits. El Niño is a supply risk for South American copper, about 36% of mine supply.
Brent forecasts are $90 for 4Q26 and $79 for 2027. Widening diesel crack spreads could keep inflation elevated even as the crude shock fades.
Europe: long peripheral Euro equities and bonds against core, plus long periphery banks. Other calls are long JGB 5s30s flattener, short USDJPY and long Taiwan equities.
Cycle-end signals are limited. Weekly jobless claims are at 219k against a 300k+ recession warning level. Corporate leverage is declining and interest coverage is healthy.
The market is shifting from macro to micro. S&P 500 correlation is at an all-time low and EPS dispersion is low, which favors stock pickers.
Utilities have derated 30% against the S&P 500 to a decade low and are priced at about a 7% yield. SG labels them the biggest upside.

market_movers.rationale: SG is short US regional banks. The report says Financials have historically lagged after Fed hikes, with a -3.4% 3-month return.

sector_views.rationale: Cheapest PEG globally, profit-driven boom, and Tech has outperformed Financials after Fed hikes.
The Fed curve favors Industrials, and SG expects reshoring, deregulation and power capex to support them.
Energy has the best 3-month sector return after Fed hikes (+6.6%), and SG raised its oil floor to $79.
Financials are the worst sector 3 months after Fed hikes (-3.4%), and SG is short regional banks.
Utilities derated 30% against the S&P 500 to a decade low, and SG calls them the biggest upside.
